definition.def: If something has a parallel, it is similar to something else, but exists or happens in a different place or at a different time. If it has no parallel or is without parallel, it is not similar to anything else.
examples: Readers familiar with English history will find a vague parallel to the suppression of the monasteries. [+ to]
It's an ecological disaster with no parallel anywhere else in the world.
...an achievement without parallel in the modern era.

definition.def: If there are parallels between two things, they are similar in some ways.
examples: Detailed study of folk music from a variety of countries reveals many close parallels.
There are significant parallels with the 1980s.
Friends of the dead lawyer were quick to draw a parallel between the two murders. [+ between]

definition.def: If one thing parallels another, they happen at the same time or are similar, and often seem to be connected.
examples: Often there are emotional reasons paralleling the financial ones. [VERB noun]
His remarks paralleled those of the president. [VERB noun]

definition.def: Parallel events or situations happen at the same time as one another, or are similar to one another.
examples: ...parallel talks between the two countries' Foreign Ministers.
Their instincts do not always run parallel with ours. [+ with]
This is a real world, running parallel to our own.

definition.def: If two lines, two objects, or two lines of movement are parallel, they are the same distance apart along their whole length.
examples: ...seventy-two ships, drawn up in two parallel lines.
Farthing Lane's just above the High Street and parallel with it. [+ with]
This trail was roughly parallel to the border.

definition.def: A parallel is an imaginary line round the Earth that is parallel to the equator. Parallels are shown on maps.
Something that occurs in parallel with something else occurs at the same time as it.
examples: Davies has managed to pursue his diverse interests in parallel with his fast-moving career. [+ with]
Progress on this issue must be made in parallel to any moves on the economic front.

examples.sentence: Others, like Michael Faraday, left extensive journals of their thoughts and speculations, parallel to their scientific notebooks.
The study covered 500 clerical employees in four parallel divisions.
If the glass were kept hot enough, it would flow over the molten tin until the top surface was also flat, horizontal and perfectly parallel to the bottom surface.
A further possibility is that of parallel universes.
Beach netting or meshing involves setting large nets parallel to the shore.
Many also had parallel ditches that collected the runoff and formed a drainage canal on each side of the road.
